title: Answer to Question: The Political and Financial Corruption Scandal Shaking the Turkish Government
text:
Answer to Question: The Political and Financial Corruption Scandal Shaking the Turkish Government

Question:

Erdogan announced on 25/12/2013 the formation of a new government, in which he changed ten ministers, after three ministers had resigned, among them the Minister of Environment, who in turn called on Erdogan to resign. This was against the background of a political and financial corruption scandal that has been shaking the Turkish government for about ten days. This had been preceded on 20/12/2013 by the arrest of 24 persons out of 49 persons close to the government and its party, who had been referred for investigation on 17/12/2013 on the charge of carrying out acts of corruption... Following that, the Prime Minister launched a harsh attack on those who caused them to be exposed and led to their arrest, and he removed dozens of security directors who are considered to be counted as belonging to the group of Fethullah Gulen, and poured the full force of his anger upon this group... He likewise directed criticism at the American ambassador in Turkey. The question is: what has newly happened so that the relationship of cooperation and support between Erdogan and the group of Fethullah Gulen has turned into a relationship of hostility? I hope that this is detailed as far as possible, as matters have become confused for us after Erdogan's actions towards that group. And then, what is the significance of Erdogan's statement towards the American ambassador, although Erdogan's relationship with America is an intimate relationship, to the extent that he is described as America's man in Turkey?

Answer:

By reviewing what took place of preliminaries and results, the answer to the above question becomes clear:

1- The announcement of these investigations and arrests provoked the government, its party and its head Erdogan, because they are directed at persons counted as belonging to the government and its ruling party, among them four sons of ministers in the government, the mayor of the Fatih district municipality in Istanbul, and the director of Halkbank... Among them also are businessmen close to this party. And it comes as Turkey approaches local elections in three months, on 30/3/2014, from which Erdogan was hoping to strengthen his popularity so as to stand for the presidency of the republic, the election for which will take place months after that, on 26/8/2014, with the voting on it by the people directly, and not as it was carried out until today, when the President of the Republic was elected by the parliament. Therefore Erdogan's reaction was very angry. He carried out changes among the security directors who are followers of the group of Fethullah Gulen, and he threatened the group's men in the judiciary, as came in the newspaper Milliyet on 18/12/2013, saying: "But those working in the field of the judiciary must respect rights and the law, and they must not move by the direction of a certain party... For no one working in the field of the judiciary has the right to rise up and exercise pressure and give orders and instructions to the executive authority in what is not customary. If you direct the judiciary in order to create a kind of pressure on the people, then we will do what we must do, and we have done it," indicating by his saying "and we have done it" the dismissal of a number of security directors... And in order for Erdogan to create sympathy for his position towards the Gulen group, he made a statement suggesting that there is a foreign conspiracy, saying: "The events that have taken place in the last days have an international extension; they are an operation by implementers at home who are subordinate to abroad," as came in the same newspaper... Then later, during his stop in Samsun during his tour to mobilise public opinion on his side, on 20/12/2013, he declared: "The ambassador is entering into the circle of some conspiratorial actions. So I direct the call to him: that he carry out his duty. If you, O ambassador, go outside the circle of your duty, then our government will go on its way to the extent that it has authority..." (Milliyet, 21/12/2013). By that he was referring to the American ambassador, commenting on news published by some Turkish newspapers, "Star, Yeni Safak and Aksam", about a meeting of the American ambassador in Ankara, Ricciardone, with some representatives of the European Union on 17/12/2013... The news carried indications of the American ambassador's interference in the events... Thus Erdogan was at the height of anger in his statements towards the Gulen group, and at the height of caution towards the American ambassador.

2- As for the Gulen group, it is known that this group supported Erdogan and his party since his assumption of power in 2002... The government allowed it to enter many institutions, in addition to its running a large number of private tutoring centres, which collected money for the group from students' fees, and at the same time prepared many of these students to work with the group... All of this was openly exposed and not secret, and Erdogan did not fear any danger from it, especially as the reality of the group is that it resembles a sheikh and his disciples, i.e., it is not a political organisation that has programmes and competes for power in order to implement them... Therefore Erdogan did not give them great attention, most especially as the group was an arm of America just as Erdogan is, even if the styles and roles differed... The two contributed to controlling the institutions and breaking the nationalist structure loyal to the British, through America being able to infiltrate the institutions by means of the group, and likewise America being able to penetrate the army and the political milieu by means of Erdogan and his party... Thus the party and the group were two arms of America in Turkey, and their relations with each other were relations of cooperation, friendship and loyalty to a single reference... This is in addition to the fact that America, at the beginning of Erdogan's rule, wanted a strong, united bloc of its men in Turkey, because the forces of the British at that time still had a remnant of influential power in the judiciary and the army which America took into account... All of this made America keen that the relations between Erdogan and his party and the group of Fethullah Gulen be clear, without tensions. The situation continued until the beginning of 2010... when events took place during that year in which the seeds of disagreement between Erdogan and Fethullah Gulen were sown. The first of them was Fethullah Gulen's message regarding the incident of the ship Marmara, which the Jewish entity attacked at dawn on 31/5/2010, where Gulen said in his message: "The sailing of the ship and its entry into Israeli territorial waters was a grave mistake, and it was necessary to obtain permission from Tel Aviv." So he faults the position of the ship, and stands beside the action of the Jewish entity and their right to kill some of its passengers, at a time when Erdogan was standing with the ship and the passengers. So Erdogan considered Fethullah Gulen's message to be directed at him personally. Nevertheless, the two got past what happened, and the relationship between them was restored to a good one. Fethullah was supportive of the referendum that Erdogan called for on 12/9/2010 on the constitutional amendments... as Fethullah Gulen had an effect in tipping the balance towards "yes" in this referendum. Gulen, from his headquarters in America, called on the Turkish people, a few weeks before the date of the referendum, to approve the constitutional amendments, explaining "that these amendments, even if limited, have what comes after them, and that they are like a point of movement towards more freedoms and democratic practice." Erdogan won this referendum, as the approval of the constitutional amendments was by a rate of 58%, and a mass celebration was held in front of the headquarters of the ruling party...

This approval resulted in a great change in the institutions, which led to filling the posts vacated of the nationalists by employing the group in them. Likewise there was a change in the structure of the Supreme Council of Judges and Prosecutors, and the newly created posts, and all of them were in favour of the group, which made it have strong influence in these effective institutions, and the group became dominant over a number of important courts and the special courts subordinate to the Supreme Council of Judges and Prosecutors.

3- Then matters became strained between them after that, with the beginning of 2011, as Erdogan noticed that the group's penetration into security and the judiciary had begun to constitute harassment of him and an attempt at domination... and not, as the matter had been before, support from the group for him. Since that time, action and reaction began alternately between Erdogan and the Gulen group:

a- Since the beginning of 2011, Erdogan began working to undermine the influence of this group. He dropped those affiliated to this group from the list of candidates for membership of parliament in the 2011 elections, then he began dismissing some of those belonging to this group from security posts and from some courts...

b- Following that, this group's media launched an attack on Erdogan... And it was not content with that; rather, it promoted what came in a recorded tape published in September 2011 about the talks of the head of the National Intelligence Organisation, Hakan Fidan, with leaders of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, Ocalan's party, in Oslo between 2009 and 2010 in order to settle the Kurdish issue. Those talks were being held at that time in secret to prepare the atmosphere before the announcement... So fingers of accusation pointed to this group as having a connection with the publication of this tape. And the chief of the public prosecution, loyal to the group, requested on 7/2/2012 the investigation of Fidan, the head of intelligence...

c- Erdogan considered this issue to be fateful for him, because it would touch the Prime Minister and reveal secrets relating to the state's contacts, through its intelligence, with the Kurdistan Workers' Party. So Erdogan fortified the head of intelligence against any legal prosecution, by having a law issued by parliament relating to that: that "it is not permitted to investigate those working in the intelligence service and persons charged with carrying out special tasks by the Prime Minister except with his permission." Following it also, Erdogan carried out a purge in the intelligence departments in Ankara, Istanbul and Izmir, and he likewise carried out purges in the education service and in the judicial service of persons counted as belonging to the Gulen group...

d- Then came the step that strongly affected the group, which is Erdogan's plan to abolish the private tutoring centres and convert them into private schools teaching the state curriculum or into secondary schools. Nearly a thousand of these centres belonged to the group, and they charge high fees from the parents of the students who attend them to strengthen their low level of education in the government schools so that they can enter the universities. The group aimed through them at two main goals: gaining money and winning these students to the group. Erdogan's government wanted to make changes in the education system, converting these centres into private schools that follow the state programme and are under its supervision, and changing the system of university entrance so that the preparatory year for university entrance after finishing secondary school is abolished, because of which many parents were forced to send their children to those centres so that they could enter the universities and obtain the high marks that enable them to enter the branch they desire. If these centres were abolished or closed, this group would lose in the two fields of gaining money and gaining individuals. For this reason the group went mad when Erdogan announced his plan to abolish these centres and convert them into private schools following the state curriculum... And it is as if the group began thinking of a reaction towards Erdogan and his party to affect his victory in the local elections that will take place in three months, on 30/3/2014.

e- After that came the corruption scandal and the arrests that included members of Erdogan's government, of his party and of those close to him... And fingers of accusation were directed at the group of Fethullah Gulen, for the reaction of the Gulen group pointed the finger of accusation at them: the group showed extreme joy at the arrests and the investigations, promoted them through its media and gloated over Erdogan... But Erdogan's rapid measures with the changes he made among the security directors, of dismissal and transfer... as he dismissed a number of security directors belonging to them... these changes turned the group's joy into sadness and grief. So it tried to obstruct or disrupt these changes and to suggest that they were illegitimate or not in force. The media supporting the group spread news that the government's decision to change security directors from July 2013 until today had been rejected by the President of the Republic and that he had not approved it. So the office of the President of the Republic immediately, on 20/12/2013, broadcast a statement issued by the President of the Republic Abdullah Gul denying the Gulen group's news... Thus the attempt of that group to show that there is a difference and disagreement between Abdullah Gul and Erdogan failed! After that the group exploded in anger at Erdogan, out of its feeling that these changes had struck it at its core. So the head of the group, Fethullah Gulen, from his headquarters in Pennsylvania in America, broadcast an angry audio speech which his group's media published on 21/12/2013, containing a supplication in which came: "...O Allah, cause the earth to swallow those who released the thieves and arrested those who pursued the thieves, and those who turned a blind eye to the criminals and tarnished the image of those who pursued the criminals; burn their houses, demolish their dwellings, scatter their gathering, cut off their root, make their violence be among themselves, and grant us victory over them..." It appears that the blow directed at his group was painful, if not back-breaking or fatal.

4- Thus matters were overturned since 2010 between Erdogan and Fethullah Gulen, and their intensity increased in the following three years until today... It appears that what the group and its head residing in Pennsylvania offered of services to America: audacity against the Deen of Allah, hostility to the system of the Khilafah, then support for America's interests until the group's last breath... all of that made Gulen think that by his services, in which he competes with Erdogan and exceeds him, he would by them gain America's pleasure, so that it would take him as a substitute for Erdogan and support him in confronting him... So he began carrying out harassments of Erdogan, as we mentioned earlier... As for the group's services to America, with which he thought that America would support him as a substitute for Erdogan and abandon Erdogan, among them are:

a- His accelerated call to the so-called moderate Islam, or rather the modified one mixed with secular and democratic ideas. He defends these ideas strongly, directs people towards them, and uses the group's media for that.

b- The group's active activity in the subject of interfaith dialogue, especially with the Jews and the Christians, and equating them with the Muslims by considering all of them believers, and its call to establish temples for them and for the Nusayris beside the mosques.

c- Its attacking all the groups calling for the establishment of the Khilafah and the Islamic State, accusing them of being extremist and terrorist, broadcasting malicious propaganda about them through the media it owns, and informing on them to the security and judicial authorities.

d- Its leader's taking the United States of America as his headquarters since 1999, and the expansion of his meetings with American officials and American intelligence... then the delivery of lectures in America containing positions, ideas and opinions that pour into the interest of the Americans. Previously he did not denounce America's invasion of Iraq and Afghanistan, and at the present time his many media outlets attack the revolutionary Islamic movements in Syria, consider them terrorist, work to tarnish their image, and support the American positions against them.

e- His positions supportive of the Jewish entity. He denounced the sending of the ship Marmara to help the people of Gaza at the end of May 2010 and gave the Jews a right to strike it, and he did not offer condolences for the Turkish victims nor consider them martyrs. Previously he denounced Saddam's striking of the entity of the Jews in 1991 and announced his pain for the Jewish dead who fell as a result of that... And his website published a picture of him, i.e., of Fethullah Gulen, meeting the chief rabbi of the Oriental Jews in the Jewish entity, Eliyahu Bakshi-Doron, in 1998.

The above services are a drop from an ocean... The group thought that by them it would attain a favour with America that would give it precedence over Erdogan, and the most likely is that this thinking of it will ruin it. For America views Erdogan, as the leader of a political party, as more capable of achieving its interests than the Gulen group with its disciples...! Furthermore, America could not achieve what it achieved inside Turkey, and the consolidation of its influence there, except by way of a political party headed by Erdogan. Therefore it supports him in order to achieve its political projects through him, especially the implementation of the American plan relating to the Kurdish issue, and the other American plans at home and abroad, among them the Syrian issue... And even if the pressures on Erdogan increased, so that he resigned for example, it is most likely that America would resort to another strong person from the Justice Party, not resort to Fethullah Gulen. That is because the reality of the group of Fethullah Gulen is that it is a non-political movement that has always sheltered under political parties, according to the saying "he is with whoever prevails". It went along with the Motherland Party of Turgut Ozal in the eighties of the last century, and afterwards it supported the Welfare Party, then the Democratic Left Party led by Ecevit in 1998 after the fall of the Welfare Party led by Erbakan, and after the Justice and Development Party was founded it rose and entered under its shade. Therefore it is viewed as being opportunist, supporting the ruling political parties in order to achieve its own special interests. Accordingly, what is expected is that it will work to reconcile with Erdogan, because it will lose if it does not do so... And this has begun to appear in the actions of the group and its followers: Gulen has retreated from the veiled attack on Erdogan, after he had described him about a month ago as Pharaoh and Nimrod, as he said in a recorded broadcast in his own voice addressing his followers, "If Pharaoh and Nimrod are against you, then you are in the right..." Then he retreated further when Gulen recently proposed that the private tutoring centres remain and be placed under the supervision of the state, in a step of concession, but Erdogan insisted on his decision... Even Fethullah's men in the judiciary and security no longer have much before them in the face of Erdogan. He has arrested numbers of them, and those who continued in their work are confused in their decisions. Some courts agreed to Erdogan's decision that the courts not accept cases directly from security directors without the approval of their superiors, and a small number of courts tried to evade the decision, as came on the private news television station "NTV" on 27/12/2013: "A high Turkish court cancelled a government decision requiring police officers to inform their superiors of investigations." Nevertheless, Sky News Arabia reported on 26/12/2013 that the public prosecutor Muammer Akkas, who is leading the investigations into corruption accusations that reached ministers in the Turkish government, said that he "faced much pressure" in this case, indicating that "the investigations were obstructed"...

And Erdogan is still threatening and menacing the group's helpers in security and the judiciary. He said during his visit to the district of Fatsa in the province of Ordu: "I direct my call to the judiciary! You say to the executive authority: clean the dirt that is among you. But you yourselves are not completely clean. And we have what we know" (Hurriyet, 21/12/2013). Thus Erdogan's position is stronger than the position of Fethullah Gulen, at least in the foreseeable future, especially as Erdogan's influence in the army has become effective. Turkish media mentioned that the Turkish Armed Forces issued a statement in which they said that they "distance themselves from any political opinions and formations and serve the Turkish nation faithfully," as came in UPI and on the Al-Hayat website on 27/12/2013.

5- As for Erdogan's allusion in his statement to the American ambassador, as published by the newspaper Milliyet on 21/12/2013, the matter is as follows:

a- During this campaign of arrests in the mentioned corruption cases... three newspapers, "Star, Yeni Safak and Aksam", published news about a meeting of the American ambassador in Ankara, Ricciardone, with some representatives of the European Union on 17/12/2013... The news carried indications of the American ambassador's interference in the events, and these newspapers claimed that the Foreign Minister Davutoglu would contact the American Secretary of State John Kerry and express to him the annoyance of the Foreign Ministry and the diplomatic corps at the ambassador's actions...

And although the American ambassador Ricciardone himself denied the claims of some of the newspapers that published this news, and denied any connection of America with the operation of arrests relating to acts of corruption, through his page on Twitter, where he said: "The United States has no connection whatsoever with the operation of arrests relating to acts of corruption, of bribes and illegitimate methods. Those reports are pure lies and fabrication. No one can expose Turkish-American relations to danger with baseless claims, and the friendship and cooperation between the two countries acquire fateful importance for the two countries" (Milliyet, 21/12/2013), Erdogan nonetheless exploited this matter, as if he had an appointment with the news of these newspapers. This led some analysts to say that it is not to be ruled out that the news was prepared for Erdogan so that he could exploit it in saying that the events have an international extension, in order to win the sympathy of the people on the basis that there is a foreign conspiracy! Accordingly, he declared during his tours to mobilise public opinion on his side... saying during his stop in Samsun on 20/12/2013: "The ambassador is entering into the circle of some conspiratorial actions. So I direct the call to him: that he carry out his duty. If you (O ambassador) go outside the circle of your duty, then our government will go on its way to the extent that it has authority" (Milliyet, 21/12/2013)... But what happened is that Davutoglu did not contact Kerry, nor did Erdogan's statement stay alive for any time; rather, the deputy chairman of the Justice and Development Party, Huseyin Celik, made the following statement: "The statement of the United States ambassador Frank Ricciardone on Twitter, in which he denies the reports relating to his statements that some newspapers published, is considered valid by us" (Hurriyet, 21/12/2013).

b- And although what is customary in states' protests against the interferences of other states is that the Foreign Ministry sends an official note of protest to the other state, or summons the ambassador... and likewise what is customary when the ambassador of any state denies news about him from the state in which he is, is that he sends a letter to the Foreign Ministry of this state in which he denies the news... what happened is that the Prime Minister issued a verbal statement... and that the American ambassador published his response on Twitter! This indicates that the "verbal sparring" between Erdogan and America is no more than a performance put on by failed actors who are not on an equal footing! And what indicates that Erdogan's "harsh" statement towards the American ambassador is much noise without grinding is that on the day on which the newspaper Milliyet published Erdogan's statement, i.e., on 21/12/2013, the same newspaper published news in which it said: (It is notable that, while the operation of pursuing corruption with an international extension continues, the American adviser responsible for intelligence relating to terrorism and finance at the US Treasury Department, David Cohen, who is known for his closeness to "Israel", arrived in Istanbul, and then meets with the directors of banks in Turkey... The adviser discusses with the directors financial matters and the sanctions on Iran... without this American official adviser meeting with any of those holding authority in the government)! This indicates that Erdogan's words are like an empty nutshell, void of meaning but which cracks loudly. For America's officials enter the country and hold discussions with whomever they wish, without meeting any Turkish official!!

c- It is known about Erdogan that he is linked to America and implements its projects inside Turkey and abroad. And these projects, especially the domestic ones, require their completion, and if he goes, they may stop... And America counts Erdogan among its strong men who have consolidated its influence in Turkey since he assumed power. Before that, British influence was the dominant one over Turkey by way of the army throughout the previous decades, ever since Mustafa Kemal abolished the Khilafah in compliance with the demand of the British, the bitter enemy of Islam and the Muslims, at the Lausanne conference, in return for their making Mustafa Kemal President of the Republic of Turkey... Since that time British influence has been dominant over government in Turkey, and America could not remove this influence, especially in the army, except after Erdogan assumed power, when British influence weakened and disappeared from the political scene, and the political parties with a British background, the most prominent of which is the People's Party, became extremely weak... Thus American influence has become the dominant one now throughout the years of Erdogan's rule, and America's influence has become present in the presidency of the republic and in the premiership... Therefore a verbal statement from Erdogan towards the American ambassador without any practical reality... such a statement America realises, and its speaker realises, to be without effect...

6- In conclusion:

a- The two poles of the current crisis in Turkey are agents of America: Erdogan and Fethullah Gulen.

b- America was concerned that Erdogan and Gulen remain one force without conflict when the British had a power that had to be taken into account. After it weakened, America kept silent about the conflict between the Justice Party and Fethullah's group, and left them to compete in loyalty to it and in serving its interests.

c- What is most likely is that Erdogan will continue, at least in the foreseeable future, for he still retains popularity. And even if the pressure on him increased, America would give preference to another person from the Justice Party over the person of Gulen, because it realises that Fethullah's group resembles a sheikh and his disciples, who must, in order to continue, shelter under a ruling political party, not himself be in government.
